span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE EXPECTED ANSWER IS STATED BEFORE IT IS OVERTURNED: on the strength of the inviscid result the authors say it seems reasonable to bet on well-posedness, and then show the equation is linearly ill-posed in that very setting
span.quote: On the basis of the inviscid result, it seems reasonable to bet for well-posedness of the Prandtl equation (1.3) in Sobolev type spaces. The aim of this paper is to show that it is actually linearly ill-posed in this framework.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the destabilisation is attributed to TWO ingredients together - viscosity, and critical points in the base velocity profile - and the authors immediately state what that conjunction buys them: the result does not contradict the positive results for the inviscid case or for monotonic data
span.quote: As we shall see later on, the reason for illposedness is a strong destabilization mechanism due to two ingredients: viscosity, and critical points in the base velocity profile. In particular, it does not contradict the positive results obtained in the inviscid case and for monotonic data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: THE PDE QUESTION IS REDUCED TO A CONDITION ON AN ORDINARY DIFFERENTIAL EQUATION: an asymptotic analysis in the high tangential frequency limit turns ill-posedness for the linearised system into a spectral condition for a reduced ODE
span.quote: It relies on an asymptotic analysis of (1.6), in the high tangential frequency limit. Thanks to this analysis, we show that ill-posedness for the PDE (1.6) comes down to a “spectral condition” for a reduced ODE, namely:

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the instability is located at a SCALE rather than at a place: it happens at high tangential frequencies with a typical time that shrinks with them, and at that timescale the time dependence of the base velocity does not matter - which lets the authors replace the real equation with a simpler frozen one
span.quote: As we shall see, it takes place at high tangential frequencies, say O(1/ε), and has a typical time O(√ε). span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A FREE PARAMETER IS ADDED TO THE ANSATZ PRECISELY BECAUSE THE SYSTEM IS OVERDETERMINED - the jump and boundary conditions supply too many constraints - and the paper says that this is what justifies introducing it
span.quote: Let us point out that this system is a priori overdetermined, as jump and boundary conditions provide too many constraints. This justifies the introduction of the parameter τ in the Ansatz (2.5).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the corrector's ROLE IS STATED AS CANCELLATION: the inviscid solution is not smooth at the critical point, and the shear layer term, which concentrates there, exists to cancel the discontinuities the regular part leaves behind
span.quote: However, it has a jump at y = a, together with its second derivative. The role of the shear layer vsl ε , which concentrates near y = a, is to cancel these discontinuities.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the sign of a second derivative would split the argument in two, and a change of variables collapses the split: if the condition holds for one sign then a transformed pair satisfies the other, so BOTH CASES yield a solution with the property the instability needs

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: WELL-POSEDNESS IN THE ANALYTIC SETTING IS PROVED IN THE SAME PAPER, as a foil: the Cauchy problem for the linearised equation is locally well-posed there, which is what makes the Sobolev result a statement about the function space rather than about the equation
span.quote: In short, the Cauchy problem for (1.6) is locally well-posed in the analytic setting.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the analytical result is accompanied by numerical computation whose stated purpose is to show the mechanism is EFFECTIVE rather than merely possible
span.quote: We end up the paper with numerical computations, which emphasize that our instability mechanism is effective.

span.label: the relevance of the asymptotics in Lp and in the absence of Rayleigh instabilities remains open
span.note: what this limits: the asymptotic result's reach: THE RELEVANCE OF THIS ASYMPTOTICS IN Lp, OR ITS RELEVANCE IN THE ABSENCE OF RAYLEIGH INSTABILITIES, ARE STILL OPEN ISSUES
span.quote: However, the relevance of this asymptotics in Lp, or its relevance in the absence of Rayleigh instabilities, are still open issues.

span.label: The negative result is confined to the viscous Sobolev setting and leaves the known positive (inviscid and monotonic-data) results intact.
span.note: what this limits: the ill-posedness result, which is confined to its setting: IT DOES NOT CONTRADICT THE POSITIVE RESULTS OBTAINED IN THE INVISCID CASE AND FOR MONOTONIC DATA
span.quote: In particular, it does not contradict the positive results obtained in the inviscid case and for monotonic data.

span.label: The originator of the model is cited as doubting that it holds uniformly, and the paper states outright that the validity of the asymptotics is not clear.
span.note: what this limits: the boundary-layer asymptotics as a description of the flow: the paper states its validity is not clear and that physicists including Prandtl himself emphasised it may not hold uniformly in space and time
span.quote: Although this formal asymptotics is very natural, its validity is not clear. As emphasized by physicists, including Prantdl himself, it may not hold uniformly in space and time

span.label: The empirical support for the description is bounded to one side of the separation zone, and the paper says which side.
span.note: what this limits: experimental agreement with the boundary-layer description: it is stated to fit many experiments upstream from the separation zone, which does not extend to the separated region
span.quote: Nevertheless, the description (1.2) fits with many experiments, upstream from the separation zone

span.label: The instability mechanism is derived with the time variation of the base velocity dropped, and carrying it back to the real system is stated to require modification.
span.note: what this limits: the mechanism as described in section 2: it is derived for a base velocity whose time variation is neglected, and accounting for the original system requires modifications
span.quote: This analysis was performed on (2.1), in which possible time variations of uswere neglected. To account for the original system (1.6) will require a few modifications, notably in the choice of the approximation

span.label: ill-posedness - LINEAR, and only that: the theorem is about the linearization around solutions with non-degenerate critical points, so the bare claim 'the Prandtl equation is ill-posed' drops the word that bounds the result
span.quote: This theorem expresses strong linear ill-posedness of the Prandtl equation in the Sobolev framework. It is a consequence of an instability process, that holds at high tangential frequencies

span.label: the expected answer - STATED AND THEN OVERTURNED: the paper records that the inviscid result made well-posedness the reasonable bet, and then proves the opposite in this framework
span.quote: On the basis of the inviscid result, it seems reasonable to bet for well-posedness of the Prandtl equation (1.3) in Sobolev type spaces. The aim of this paper is to show that it is actually linearly ill-posed in this framework

span.label: the source of instability - VISCOSITY, which is the term usually read as stabilising: the paper names viscosity and critical points in the base profile as the two ingredients
span.quote: As we shall see later on, the reason for illposedness is a strong destabilization mechanism due to two ingredients: viscosity, and critical points in the base velocity profile

span.label: extends → prior well-posedness results for the Prandtl equation (analytic or monotone data)
span.quote: This problem is known to be well-posed for analytic data [13, 10], or for data with monotonicity properties [11, 15].

span.label: builds-on → reference [8] (analysis of the inviscid version of the Prandtl equation)
span.quote: Interestingly, the strong instability is due to vicosity, which is coherent with well-posedness results obtained for the inviscid version of the equation [8].

span.label: builds-on → reference [8] (study of the inviscid spectral problem and its evolution equation)
span.quote: This spectral problem, as well as the corresponding evolution equation, have been studied exhaustively in [8].

span.label: The Cauchy problem for the Prandtl boundary-layer equation is LINEARLY ILL-POSED in Sobolev-type spaces (though well-posed for analytic or monotone data), proven by constructing unstable quasimodes at high tangential frequencies around solutions with non-degenerate critical points.
span.quote: We prove here that it is linearly ill-posed in Sobolev type spaces. The key of the analysis is the construction, at high tangential frequencies, of unstable quasimodes for the linearization around solutions with non-degenerate critical points.

span.label: Strikingly, the strong instability is caused by VISCOSITY — consistent with well-posedness of the inviscid version of the equation.
span.quote: the strong instability is due to vicosity, which is coherent with well-posedness results obtained for the inviscid version of the equation
